title: Quorum-based cross-region readiness gating with decay windows and traffic-weighted circuit breakers
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Production problem: During multi-region failovers and partial-network degradations, aggressive readiness probe failures in one region cause the global autoscaler to rebalance or shed capacity, creating cascading request failures and SLO violations. Proposal: implement a quorum-based readiness evaluation that factors local probe results, synthetic health samples, recent tail-latency percentiles, and a decay window before flipping node readiness. Complement with traffic-weighted circuit breakers and probabilistic probe suppression to avoid synchronized transitions. Goals: reduce autoscaler thrash, maintain p99 SLO during region perturbations, and provide observable signals for runbook actions.
background: We currently mark instances not-ready on single probe failures which makes autoscaler treat capacity as lost immediately.
Observed failure modes: network blips, transient GC pauses, short-lived kernel stalls that recover within seconds but cause autoscaler thrash and request retries across regions.
Existing mitigations (probe smoothing, cooldowns) reduce noise but don't prevent correlated cascading behavior during region-level issues.
acceptance_criteria: New readiness evaluation reduces regional readiness flips by >= 70% under injected 10s network blips in chaos tests.
End-to-end SLO regressions under synthetic failovers <= 5% increase in p99 tail relative to baseline.
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-customer; logs and metrics emitted for every readiness decision.
implementation_plan: Design quorum algorithm and decay window rules; define metric thresholds (p95, p99, error rate) used for gating.
Add synthetic sampler that issues internal low-cost requests to warm KV caches and validate forward progress.
Implement probabilistic suppression: when multiple nodes fail probes simultaneously, only mark a fraction as not-ready immediately; others enter guarded mode.
Extend autoscaler to honor node readiness grace-periods and traffic-weight weights when calculating scale events.
Add circuit breaker layer that can be traffic-weighted per-route and back-pressures region routing based on live readiness quorum.
Create feature flag and rollout plan: rollout to non-prod -> subset of customers -> global.

runbook_notes: If quorum fails and traffic-weighted circuit breaker trips, shift traffic to next healthy region and notify oncall.
Rollback: disable readiness-quorum feature flag for affected region; allow autoscaler to revert to previous behavior.
Post-incident: collect probe traces, p99 latency snapshots, and autoscaler decision logs for one hour before/after.
notes: This approach prioritizes reducing correlated readiness flips over immediate removal of unhealthy nodes. Tradeoffs: slight increase in tail latency for short windows while nodes recover vs. broad flapping that causes routing churn. We'll validate in chaos runs and a small customer canary before wider rollout.
